item.title: 5-star SF DeMarcus Henry commits to North Carolina
item.description: Five-star small forward DeMarcus Henry , one of the top players in the 2027 class, has committed to North Carolina and coach Michael Malone, he announced on NBA Today. The 6-foot-7 small forward out of Compass Prep (AZ) chose the Tar Heels over Arkansas, Louisville, Kentucky, and others. [ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ] Henry, a native of Charlotte, NC, is ranked as the No. 3 overall recruit in the 2027 class, according to the Rivals Industry Ranking , an average of all three major recruiting media companies (Rivals, ESPN, 247Sports). Rivals’ evaluators are higher on him, ranking him No. 2 nationally. Henry on North Carolina In a previous interview with Rivals, DeMarcus Henry discussed the North Carolina program. UNC : “I’m starting to get to know Coach (Michael) Malone , who is coming from the NBA. He’s a great coach, and he talks to me about NBA-style basketball, which I like. They’ve been recruiting me hard for a long time, so that means a lot.” More on Henry DeMarcus Henry is the son of the late Chris Henry , a former wide receiver for the Cincinnati Bengals. His older brother, Chris Henry Jr. , is a five-star freshman wide receiver at Ohio State, while his sister, Seini Henry , plays basketball for the Buckeyes. Henry has been one of the biggest stock risers in the 2027 class this summer. In June, he earned First Team honors at the NBPA Top 100 Camp after leading the event in both scoring (20.0 PPG) and rebounding (9.3 RPG). He also was named to the USA Basketball U18 National Team, helping the United States win a silver medal. Scouting Henry Rivals’ national recruiting analyst Jamie Shaw has evaluated DeMarcus Henry multiple times. Here is what he’s recently written about him: Demarcus Henry has such good feel for simply going to get the ball. The lefty seems to consistently make plays using his length, pop, and instincts. Henry brings consistent defensive presence, scaling up and down a lineup. Offensively, he is still growing but finishes plays around the basket. The hustle plays stood out for Henry. Using his length, twitch, and anticipation, he seemed to always find himself around the ball. An instinctive rebounder, he corralled missed shots in and out of his area. Offensively, Henry was at his best filling the lanes in transition. He switched ends with a purpose and finished at the rim. The offensive game will need to continue expanding, but you love the ability to consistently make positive plays on both ends of the floor.

item.title: Leclerc fastest in Mexico City Grand Prix first practice
item.description: Charles Leclerc went fastest in a practice session featuring 10 rookie drivers [Reuters] Ferrari's Charles Leclerc led Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli in first practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix, where the Italian is poised to clinch his first world title. Leclerc was 0.659 seconds quicker than Antonelli, for whom a ninth-place finish will secure the championship regardless of any other results. Only a victory by his team-mate George Russell or Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton can theoretically stop Antonelli becoming champion on Sunday. Even then, Antonelli only needs ninth place if Russell wins and 10th if Hamilton does. Third quickest in the session was Mercedes reserve Frederik Vesti, driving Russell's car, ahead of Hamilton. Mercedes were one of 10 teams to choose this session to do one of their mandatory rookie sessions. Only Ferrari had both race drivers in their cars. Mexico City is chosen by many teams to run their mandatory rookie sessions because the first session is traditionally unrepresentative as a result of the dirty track surface. Japanese Ayumu Iwasa, in for Max Verstappen at Red Bull, was fifth fastest, ahead of Alpine's Pierre Gasly and Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso. McLaren's Oscar Piastri, Haas driver Oliver Bearman and Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad completed the top 10. Briton Freddie Slater's first outing at a grand prix weekend for Audi did not go to plan. Reliability problems limited his running to 14 laps - about half a standard mileage. But he did manage to get out for the final 20 minutes or so and set the 19th fastest time. He was just behind another Briton, Luke Browning having his latest run in the Williams. Colton Herta, who Cadillac are considering promoting to F1 next year in place of Valtteri Bottas, was 22nd. The team believe he has now done enough miles to secure the 40 points he needs to secure the superlicence required to run in F1. item.title: Eagles Pass On Trading Moro Ojomo Despite Contract Year
item.description: Matt Marton-Imagn Images The Philadelphia Eagles are sending a clear message to the rest of the NFL: they will not sell Moro Ojomo. Despite the team’s 2-5 record and the trade deadline on November 10, the front office has not traded the fourth-year player who was a seventh-round pick. Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reported that the Eagles have received multiple calls regarding the defensive tackle, yet the team has told other clubs that Ojomo is not available. This stance comes as a surprise to many observers who expected the Eagles to be sellers. The team has already committed significant money to fellow defensive linemen Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis. Still, the organization seems ready to pay Ojomo as well, even with those massive contracts already in place. Breer noted that the team has given off the vibe that it will try to re-sign Ojomo despite the financial tightrope. A Rising Star in a Contract Year Ojomo is in the final year of his rookie deal, which usually makes a player prime trade bait for contenders. He posted a career-high six sacks last season and has shown the ability to get to the quarterback. The Eagles could have used the assets from the trade to help a win‑now team while clearing cap space for themselves. Instead, they appear focused on keeping their defensive line intact for the long haul. Other contract-year players like Hollywood Brown, Tariq Woolen, and Dallas Goedert could be available for trade, but Ojomo is off the table. Quinyon Mitchell, anticipated to rank among the league’s top-paid cornerbacks, requires the team to ready a substantial payment. Cooper DeJean also seems likely to secure a new deal soon. While Ojomo has the potential to follow the path of Milton Williams, who signed for $104 million with New England, his production this season has not matched that high price tag yet. Current Stats and Defensive Role Ojomo has played in all seven games so far this season. He has recorded 18 tackles, two tackles for loss, and generated 16 total pressures. However, he does not have a sack this season. PFF advanced metrics indicate an overall defensive grade of 53.9, placing him 83rd out of 126 eligible interior defensive linemen. His pass-rush grade sits at 53.9 as well, placing him 110th out of the same group. Despite the lower grades, the defensive coordinator sees value in the player. Vic Fangio has praised Ojomo’s effort and speed in previous comments. “He’s active, gives great effort. He’s quick, fast. He’s gotten dinged a couple of times, which has affected his play. He got a little something this past game, but he’s playing good,” Fangio said. This positive internal view likely drives the decision to keep him rather than trade him away. The front office believes he can still become a key part of their rotation alongside Carter and Davis. If Ojomo can improve his pass-rush numbers in the remaining weeks, he could justify a large extension next spring.

item.title: ASU offense, quarterback Jake Fette prepare for scary Halloween clash at BYU
item.description: Arizona State freshman quarterback Jake Fette looks to throw in the third quarter against Kansas State at Mountain America Stadium in Tempe, Ariz., on Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026. (Photo by Madison Sorenson/Cronkite News) TEMPE – Arizona State coach Kenny Dillingham is set to throw freshman quarterback Jake Fette into a figurative fire on Saturday. Because Fette’s childhood days aren’t too far behind him, memories of dressing up for Halloween and trick-or-treating might be fresh in his mind, but Fette is set to face something much scarier than any decoration or costume this year on Halloween. When the Sun Devils meet No. 8 BYU at Lavell Edwards Stadium in Provo, Utah, they’ll do so against more than 62,000 fans, hungry for a win after an upset loss at Central Florida the previous week. Adding to the challenge is the Cougars defense, which ranks 26th in the nation in scoring defense (18.57 points) and 23rd in total defense (301.6 yards), the latter of which ranks second in the Big 12. BYU (6-1, 3-1 Big 12) is on an 11-game winning streak at home, dating back almost two years. In their most recent home game, the Cougars took down then-No. 2 Notre Dame 28-24 with a goal-line stand, ending the Fighting Irish’s 16-game winning streak. While leading a team into Provo isn’t easy for any quarterback, it’s even harder for a player making his first collegiate start, and only the third appearance of his college career. Based on practices this week, last week’s starter, sixth-year quarterback Mikey Keene, looks unfit to start Saturday. Even with that knowledge, Dillingham said he can’t fully prepare Fette for BYU. “This is one of the best, most consistent fan bases in college football,” Dillingham said. “This is one of the best, most consistent coaching staffs in college football. When you have the consistency that they have as a program from the top … I don’t think there is a way to (prepare him).” After Keene went down with an injury near the end of the second half and Cutter Boley, who started the first six games of the season, had an underwhelming third quarter, Fette played the fourth quarter last week in a comeback win against Kansas State. The energy inside Mountain America Stadium flipped after Fette entered the game. While the El Paso, Texas, native only completed 3 of 6 passes for 45 yards, the Sun Devils scored two touchdowns with Fette on the field, winning the game 28-17. As he prepared his young quarterback to enter that game, Dillingham had a simple message. “It’s football,” Dillingham said. “You’ve been doing this since you were 6 years old. item.title: Red Sox news: Sonny Gray officially entering free agency after mutual option decision
item.description: Daniel Kucin Jr.-Imagn Images Red Sox news: Sonny Gray officially entering free agency after mutual option decision appeared first on ClutchPoints . The Boston Red Sox ’ starting pitcher Sonny Gray is officially entering free agency after his $30 million mutual option for the 2027 season was declined. The decision means that his stay with Boston is now set to come to an end after just one year , with the success he had in the previous season now likely to result in a more lucrative multi-year contract. Gray is now set to receive a $10 million buyout and is officially a free agent, per a post on X by Tim Healey. The 36-year-old finished 18-5 with a 2.72 ERA, 1.15 WHIP and 149 strikeouts across 169 innings in 29 starts. The 18 victories tied Gray with Philadelphia Phillies starter Cristopher Sánchez for the most in MLB. The mutual option was worth $30 million, but neither side appeared particularly interested in exercising it. Gray’s departure from St. Louis last November proved beneficial for both the pitcher and Boston. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) With the Cardinals beginning a rebuild, the veteran right-hander agreed to waive his no-trade clause to facilitate a move to the Red Sox. He subsequently became an important part of Boston’s rotation, particularly in the continued absence of Garrett Crochet. Last season, Gray recorded a 6.7% walk rate, a 33.2% chase rate, and generated ground balls on 46.4% of balls in play. He also pitched at least six innings in 22 of his 29 starts, and is likely to generate interest from a number of teams in free agency. Now, Gray is set to enter his 15th MLB season and will turn 37 in November, which is likely to play a major factor in the impending negotiations. However, his 2026 production means that he is likely to receive substantial interest as a free agent. The Red Sox are set to get a five-day exclusive negotiating window, with Gray one of the three players to enter free agency, alongside Patrick Sandoval and Isiah Kiner-Falefa. item.description: Barcelona injury crisis hands out-of-favour star a potential lifeline to save his career Barcelona’s defensive injury crisis has left Hansi Flick with some difficult decisions ahead of the upcoming fixtures. However, while the manager continues to navigate a shortage of fully fit defenders, one player has received an opportunity that could make or break his career at the club. Alejandro Balde could be in line to feature for Barça against Deportivo Alaves, potentially starting for the first time this season. Having spent much of his time on the sidelines, the 23-year-old finally has a chance to convince Flick that he deserves an important role in his plans. From undisputed starter to forgotten option Balde’s decline in importance has been particularly surprising considering his standing within the squad not long ago. During the 2025/26 campaign, the La Masia graduate made 42 appearances, including 31 starts. However, Flick’s preference for other options this season has completely changed his situation at the club. The German manager even left Balde out of the squad for Barcelona’s season opener against Elche, suggesting that the defender was not fully prepared and needed to clear his mind. Since then, opportunities have been extremely limited. Before Sunday’s Clasico , Balde had played just 12 minutes against Racing Santander and another 16 against PSG. Balde’s prominence has faded drastically this season. (Photo by Yasser Bakhsh/Getty Images) He has been an unused substitute in seven league matches this season. His last competitive start came against Valencia on May 23, more than five months ago. Despite interest from Manchester United during the summer, Balde chose to stay, determined to prove himself at Barcelona. Defensive injuries open an unexpected door The situation has now changed dramatically following injuries to Xavi Espart, Eric Garcia, Andreas Christensen and Jules Kounde. Espart faces approximately seven weeks out after suffering an ankle injury against Real Madrid, while Kounde has also been ruled out of the Alaves encounter. Balde replaced Espart during the Clasico and played around 60 minutes, marking his first substantial involvement of the season. With Joao Cancelo potentially needed to fill in at right-back, Balde could occupy his natural position on the left against Alaves. Beyond that, Barcelona face Aston Villa and Atletico Madrid before the international break. These matches could provide an opportunity for Balde to rebuild his confidence. item.title: Mazzulla Backs Sports Science After Tatum’s 42-minute Back-To-Back Grind
item.description: Winslow Townson-Imagn Images On the second night of a back-to-back, Jayson Tatum scored 40 points in 42 minutes. That is not a recipe for a championship. It is a recipe for a broken body. But Joe Mazzulla did not blink. He watched his star play until the buzzer against the Brooklyn Nets and then doubled down on the plan. The Celtics won 125-124 in overtime, but the victory came with a heavy cost in wear and tear. This was a gamble that could define the entire season. The coaching staff knew the risk. They also knew they had to trust their data. Mazzulla told reporters that this specific moment is where the team relies on their sports science team. He said, “This is where you trust Nick [Sang] and our sports science team. This is where you build [with rotations and shift length]…because you know nights like this are gonna come up.” That quote changes how we view the roster. It is not just about talent. It is about managing the body. The Shift in Physical Play The old way of thinking focused on size and bulk. That approach is dead in the modern NBA. Former Celtics strength coach Bryan Doo explained the change years ago. He noted that “pure size and mass isn’t the big thing anymore.” The game has become faster. It relies on speed and movement patterns rather than just brute force. Doo added, “It’s a quick game.” This shift explains why Tatum can play heavy minutes without collapsing. His body mechanics fit the new style. Yet, the minutes still add up. The team played 48 minutes of regulation plus overtime. Tatum was on the floor for 42 of them. That is an incredible load for a player who needs to last 82 games. When reviewing film, Mazzulla admitted the team would treat this win as a loss. The sloppy play and turnovers were a warning sign. They added more miles to the odometer early in the season. Trusting the Data Over the Gut Why did they not rest Tatum? The answer lies in the medical staff’s history. Against the 76ers in a Game 7 last spring, this same group sat Tatum out. They made a tough call then to protect the star. Now, they are making the opposite call to win a regular-season game. Mazzulla explained the logic after the win against the Nets. He said, “At the end of the day, it’s two-fold. We trust the sports science team that we have. We trust the competition of those guys.” This trust extends to the whole roster. The team used younger players like Baylor Scheierman and Payton Pritchard to start overtime. They returned to the floor after a rough two-minute stretch. The coaching staff believes the depth can handle the pressure. Assistant coach Gonzalez noted, according to CelticsBlog , “We’ve got a lot of good players that have proven that they can play at a high level and contribute to the team at any certain point.” The system relies on this depth to survive the grind. The Road Ahead for Boston The Celtics face a brutal schedule ahead. Back-to-backs will happen again. The league is full of traps for teams that do not manage their minutes.

item.title: Why Pirates need to re-sign Brandon Lowe
item.description: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 23: Brandon Lowe #5 of the Pittsburgh Pirates watches his hit go for a solo home run during the second inning against the St. Louis Cardinals at PNC Park on September 23, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Pirates are getting ready for the offseason after the conclusion of the World Series earlier this week. The team has an intriguing free agency period upcoming, as an impending lockout could stall progress during the offseason for weeks and possibly months. When free agency does get going, the Pirates will have a big decision to make regarding second baseman Brandon Lowe, who is one of the top free agent bats in the league, according to Tim Kelly of Bleacher Report. “It’s difficult to project how owner Bob Nutting will act, but the right move for the Pirates would be to extend the one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer to Lowe. If he accepts it, you get a really good player for another season. If he declines it, his market could be suppressed enough that you re-sign him, or you’ll get draft-pick compensation if he leaves in free agency,” Kelly wrote. “Given he’s 32 and has dealt with injuries before, Lowe should decline the QO if the Pirates extend him and take the best long-term deal he can get. He’s not going to have a better contract year than he did in 2026.” The only players ranked higher on Kelly’s list are New York Mets infielder Bo Bichette, Teruaki Sato, Seiya Suzuki, and Randy Arozarena of the Seattle Mariners. The Pirates retaining Lowe would be a major boost to their playoff momentum that they’ve built over the last couple of years. If they don’t bring him back, there will be a massive hole in the lineup. If they replace Lowe with someone of equal or similar caliber, it might save things, but bringing him back in particular would be the best possible route for a team that wants to keep continuity moving forward. item.title: Brewers celebrate World Series triumph with parade
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers outfielder Sal Frelick, center, celebrated with fans in the stands at the Green Bay Packers NFL game ahead of a parade where thouands of fans gathered to pay tribute to the Brewers' victory in the 2026 World Series (Stacy Revere) The Milwaukee Brewers celebrated their first World Series triumph on Friday with a rowdy parade as hundreds of thousands of supporters basked in the glow of of a hard-earned crown. City officials said they expected a total of 400,000 people would line the streets for a bus trip through the downtown streets and a victory celebration at a city park including Major League Baseball's championship trophy. "I'm on top of the world," said Brewers outfielder Sal Frelick. "It doesn't get any better. Look at these people. It's so special." Frelick screamed and waved at the crowd while holding the trophy and marveling at the passion of the fans who backed the club as it won an MLB-best 103 regular-season games then dominated in a playoff run. "This is unbelievable. One of the best days of my life, seriously," said Frelick, who promised fans, "I'm going to have a beer for every single person here." It had been a wild 48 hours for Frelick, who helped the Brewers win the World Series on Wednesday night, jumped into the stands at Lambeau Field at an NFL game Thursday in an impromptu version of the Green Bay Packers famed "Lambeau Leap" then joined the party parade on Friday. Fans began filling a park for the victory celebration five hours before it began, with many youth on hand as schools were closed for the day in the area. World Series Most Valuable Player William Contreras drew huge cheers on the celebration stage, leading supporters in "M-V-P" chants. "It's awesome," Brewers captain Christian Yelich said. "Everybody has waited a really long time for this. "We're just really excited we could bring that trophy home in Milwaukee and share it with everybody that's out here today." It was not the first time Milwaukee celebrated a World Series champion, although it had been almost 70 years since it happened. The 1957 Milwaukee Braves beat the New York Yankees in seven games for the team's first title since 1914 when they were based in Boston. The Braves moved to Atlanta for the 1966 campaign, setting the stage for the Brewers 1970 debut. Milwaukee fans also held a parade for the 1982 Brewers even though they lost to St. Louis in seven games in the club's only prior World Series appearance. js/rcw

item.title: Dakar Rally Heads to Portugal and Morocco for 2027
item.description: From Algarve to Marrakech Photo by Honda. The 49th Dakar Rally has found its home, as organizers have confirmed the 2027 edition will run from Portugal to Morocco. The move marks a genuine return to the event's roots, bringing the rally back to Africa for the first time in two decades. The relocation is a direct response to security concerns in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia , where Iran-backed Houthi strikes prompted the Amaury Sport Organisation and Saudi Motorsport Company to move the event. Both bodies called the decision "exceptional and one-off." Saudi Arabia is still slated to host the milestone 50th edition in 2028. Running January 9 to 23, the route opens with a prologue and the first special stage in Algarve, Portugal, starting from Loulé-Faro and the 30,000-seat Algarve Stadium. That venue is familiar territory for the Rally community, having hosted a World Rally-Raid Championship round in recent seasons under the Automóvel Club de Portugal. After the opening special, the caravan transfers to the port for an overnight Mediterranean crossing to Nador, Morocco. Morocco carries the bulk of the workload, hosting eleven stages plus the Agadir rest day. From the first bivouac in Bouarfa, the route heads south along the Atlas Mountains through Zagora before the 24-hour break in Agadir. The second week pushes into the sparsely traveled deserts of the far south. Smara and a run almost all the way to Dakhla stand as the route's deepest points. From there, the caravan turns back north along the Atlantic coast to finish in Marrakech. Photo by Edo Bauer. The full route spans roughly 4,862 miles across six bivouacs, including about 2,698 miles of special stage racing, distances close to recent editions of the Dakar Rally. Most specials run between roughly 217 and 311 miles per day, with the longest tests topping 300 miles of racing. "The relocated 49th edition of the Dakar will meet the sporting standards that have always made it the most demanding rally-raid event," said Race Director David Castera. "Despite the short timeframe we have had to work with, we have designed a true Dakar." With 350 competitors already registered and broadcasts in more than 190 countries, the 49th Dakar arrives as the opening round of the 2027 FIA and FIM World Rally-Raid Championships. Uwe Rösler decided to make a first-half substitution to avoid a potential second booking for 18-year-old Meyer as former Arsenal youngster Charlie Patino entered in his place. item.title: Koepka Blasts AimPoint Putting As Tour Greens Turn To Dust
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Brooks Koepka has finally said what many golf fans have been whispering for years. The five-time major champion is not a fan of the AimPoint system, and he is speaking up about the physical toll it takes on the course. During an appearance on Dan Rapaport’s show this week, Koepka pointed directly at the green damage caused by the routine. The situation was called a mess of footprints and scuff marks right around the cup. The issue is not about how long players take to read a putt. It is about where they stand while doing it. Koepka noted that the circle within three feet of the hole is getting chewed up. He explained that caddies and players are stepping on that exact spot too often. “How dried out and firm it is from three feet around the hole, I don’t know if it’s because guys are doing AimPoint more… the caddies are in there,” Koepka said, according to Yahoo Sports . This observation shifts the debate from time management to turf health. The Routine Creates the Damage The mechanics of AimPoint explain why the wear is so concentrated. A player straddles the line to feel the slope, then spins to calculate the aim point with his fingers. Koepka described the motion as a simple turn. “You go this way, then you spin and do the other way,” he said. The problem is that this routine now happens right next to the hole instead of in the middle of the fairway. Players are running the same strip of turf over and over again during a Sunday round. Historically, AimPoint arguments focused on slowing down the game. This new critique focuses on the physical condition of the playing surface. Koepka admits he cannot fully separate the two issues, but the visual evidence is clear. A single player occupies a position while another takes up residence directly behind him on that identical line, which he has observed. The result is a hole surrounded by dead grass. “It’s very chewed up around the green,” Koepka told Rapaport, per Yahoo Sports. A Complicated History It is ironic that Koepka is leading this charge since he used the technique himself. To verify his putting reads and protect his knees, he began using AimPoint prior to the 2021 Ryder Cup. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-USA TODAY Sports “The Brow’s” legacy in New Orleans had many layers. He was the hope of the city, the face of the franchise, and ultimately the villain who forced his way out of a franchise. His turn from being the sweetheart of the “big easy” to the complete villain is worth studying. Davis was drafted first overall in the 2012 NBA Draft by the New Orleans Hornets. The franchise was renamed the New Orleans Pelicans the following season. Before entering the NBA, he played one year at the University of Kentucky, winning an NCAA championship in a legendary season under coach John Calipari. He was a breath of fresh air for a franchise that had lost its star player, Chris Paul , a few seasons earlier. During his time in the Big Easy, Davis was easily a top 10 player in the league. His seven-foot-five wingspan made him a nightmare in the paint, and he averaged 2.4 blocks per game.
